subject.title: Feature: configurable bootstrap file injection order for prompt cache optimization

question: Should OpenClaw accept `bootstrapDynamicFiles`/`bootstrapFileOrder` as a core config surface, or expose this control through a context-engine/plugin hook contract instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding user-controlled bootstrap ordering and volatility classification creates a durable prompt-cache and config API that automation should not choose.

options.title: Accept narrow core config
options.body: Add `bootstrapDynamicFiles` and optional `bootstrapFileOrder` with unchanged defaults, schema/docs/tests, and explicit prompt-cache semantics.

options.title: Extend context/plugin contract
options.body: Add or document a minimal context-engine or plugin API for ordering and dynamic-file classification instead of putting new knobs in core config.

options.title: Decline new control
options.body: Keep the fixed heartbeat-only dynamic split and document operational guidance for volatile workspace files.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow core config
recommendation.body: Add `bootstrapDynamicFiles` and optional `bootstrapFileOrder` with unchanged defaults, schema/docs/tests, and explicit prompt-cache semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the best available decision owner from the history because his adjacent bootstrap-cache and AI runtime work is closest to the product/API contract choice.
